mainTopic: Walls made of people (knowingly versus unknowingly), and a משנה about someone who left his תחום with permission, leading to the debate over הבלעת תחומין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about using a person as a wall (מחיצה). The גמרא settles two ברייתות that seem to clash: a person who knows he is serving as a wall does not count, but a person who does not know does count. It defends this rule using the story of רבי נחמיה and רב חסדא. Then it tells stories that show the rule in practice: שמואל flogged a wedding party that used people who knew, רבא forbade a repeat with the flasks in מחוזא, and several חכמים had things brought to them through walls of people who did not know. A new משנה follows about a man who left his תחום with permission and was told his trip was no longer needed. רבה and רב שימי בר חייא explain differently what 'within the limit, it is as if he never left' means. The גמרא shows that their argument rests on whether הבלעת תחומין, the overlapping of שבת limits, counts. אביי challenges רבה from a cave case, רבה answers by pointing to partitions set before שבת, and אביי begins to push back, with the discussion continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: The person-versus-person contradiction remains
steps.stepSummary: After solving the contradiction about objects, the גמרא says the contradiction about people is still a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the contradiction between the ruling about a person and the other ruling about a person is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one contradiction is still open: one ברייתא says a person may not serve as a wall, and another says he may. This line sets up the next move, an answer to this contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer just given for objects (כלי אכלי) does not help with people. One ברייתא forbids using a person as a דופן. The other allows a person to make his friend a דופן so he can eat, drink and sleep in the סוכה. So the גמרא needs a new way to tell the two cases apart.

keyTerms.meaning: but / however (turning to a remaining problem)
a person against a person: a ruling about people that contradicts another ruling about people
it is difficult; there is a contradiction

phrases.english: But a person against a person is difficult!
phrases.notes: The two ברייתות about using a person as a wall seem to say opposite things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier answer to the object-versus-object contradiction and turns to the person-versus-person contradiction that is still open.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about whether a person can serve as a wall (מחיצה/דופן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source forbids using a person as a wall and the other allows it, and the answer given for objects does not solve this.

steps.title: Knowingly versus unknowingly
steps.stepSummary: A person who knows he is serving as a wall does not count. A person who does not know does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The person-versus-person contradiction is also not difficult. Here, the case is where he knows. Here, the case is where he does not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by setting each ברייתא in a different case. The ruling that forbids is about someone who knowingly serves as a wall. The ruling that allows is about someone who serves as a wall without knowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות are about people, but they describe different situations. When the person knows he is being used as a wall, he is not counted as a wall. When he is placed there without knowing it, he does count as a wall. So the two sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: this is also not difficult
here... here: each source is about a different case
knowingly; with the person's awareness
unknowingly; without the person's awareness

steps.whatToRemember: A person who knowingly stands as a wall does not count as a מחיצה. A person who unknowingly stands as one does count.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the answer the גמרא gave for objects. Here the deciding factor is whether the person knows he is serving as a wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: The next two challenges test this exact rule, so it is the basis for the rest of the passage.

phrases.english: A person against a person is also not difficult:
here, knowingly; here, unknowingly.
phrases.notes: The 'knowingly' case is the ברייתא that forbids it. The 'unknowingly' case is the one that allows it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source is about a different case (כאן... כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about whether a person can ever be a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not knowing he is a wall: he counts. Knowing he is a wall: he does not count.

steps.title: Challenge from the story of רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: In the story of רבי נחמיה בריה דרבי חנילאי, the people seem to have known they were forming a wall, yet it worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the case of רבי נחמיה, son of רבי חנילאי, was a case of knowingly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer using the earlier story of רבי נחמיה. In that story, people were used as a wall for him, and the גמרא assumes they knew what they were doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 2 says that a knowing person cannot count as a wall. In the רבי נחמיה story a human wall was relied on, and it looks like the people did it knowingly. If so, that story goes against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: but look at; introduces a case that seems to contradict
it was

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִילַאי,
phrases.english: But the case of Rabbi Neḥemya, son of Rabbi Ḥanilai,
phrases.notes: This is the story told just before, where רב חסדא had people stand as a wall for רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: was knowingly!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִילַאי לְדַעַת הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 2 against an earlier story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person who knowingly stands as a wall does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the רבי נחמיה story a human wall worked even though the people seemingly knew they were a wall.

steps.title: The people in that story did not know
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the people who formed the wall for רבי נחמיה did not know it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a case of unknowingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people in the רבי נחמיה story did not know they were serving as a wall. So the story fits the rule from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the people knew. The גמרא rejects that assumption and says they were made into a wall without knowing it. That puts the story in the 'unknowingly' category, where a person does count as a wall.

phrases.english: It was unknowingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the facts of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The people knew they were a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The people did not know, so they fit the 'unknowingly' case.

steps.title: But רב חסדא knew
steps.stepSummary: Even if the others did not know, רב חסדא, who arranged the wall, certainly knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא, at least, was knowingly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: even if the other people did not know, רב חסדא was the one who arranged the wall, so he knew. That seems to bring back the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 covers the people who did not know. It does not cover רב חסדא himself, who was aware. If he was part of the wall, then a knowing person was part of a wall that worked.

keyTerms.meaning: at least; in any case

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda, at least, was knowingly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 by pointing to one person who clearly did know.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the wall in the רבי נחמיה story was made unknowingly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא arranged the wall and so knew. If he was part of it, a knowing person helped form a valid wall.

steps.title: רב חסדא was not one of the people making up the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא knew, but he was not counted among the people who formed the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא was not part of the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא was not one of the people who made up the wall. So the fact that he knew does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall was made only of people who did not know. רב חסדא knew, but he was not counted as part of the wall itself. This shows the rule is about the people who actually form the wall. Because of this answer, the rule from step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: not part of the count; not one of the people counted as forming the wall

steps.whatToRemember: Only the people who actually make up the wall need to be unaware. Someone who knows but is not part of the wall does not ruin it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא, שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמִּנְיָן הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda was not part of the count.
phrases.notes: He means רב חסדא was not one of the people who stood as the wall itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמִּנְיָן הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and closes this line of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting who counts as part of the wall
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא was part of the wall, so a knowing person helped form it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא was not counted in the wall. Only unaware people formed it, so the rule of step 2 stands.

steps.title: שמואל punishes a wedding party for using a wall of people who knew
steps.stepSummary: A wedding party brought water in through a wall of people who knew they were a wall. שמואל had them flogged, because a wall of people only works when they do not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a wedding party that brought water in through a wall made of people. שמואל had them flogged. He said: if the חכמים allowed it when the people do not know, does that mean they would allow it when the people do know?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the rule from step 2 in action. When the people knew they were a wall, שמואל treated it as forbidden and punished them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a person who knows he is a wall does not count. Here we see how seriously this was taken: שמואל did not just say it fails, he punished them. His logic is simple: permission for the case where people do not know cannot be stretched to the case where they do.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of a wedding party
A wall made of people standing together
He had them flogged
Without knowing / knowingly

phrases.english: There were these members of a wedding party
who brought water in
through a wall made of people.
phrases.notes: The people standing there knew they were being used as a wall. That is why it was a problem.

phrases.english: שמואל had them flogged.
He said: If they said it works when the people do not know,
would they say it works when the people know?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי גְנָנָא דְּאַעִילוּ מַיָּא בִּמְחִיצָה שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 3 through 6 defended the rule from step 2, this story shows the rule being applied in practice.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wall of people who know they are a wall does not work and is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שמואל flogging the wedding party, and his reasoning.

steps.title: רבא allows the flasks once but forbids it the next week
steps.stepSummary: Flasks in the market of מחוזא were brought in for רבא while a crowd walked with him. The next week רבא forbade it, because now people would know they were a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some flasks lying in the market of מחוזא. When רבא came back from his lecture, they brought the flasks in for him. On another שבת they wanted to bring them in again, but רבא forbade it. He said it is now like the case where the people know, and so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story. The first time worked because the crowd did not know they were being used as a wall. The second time was forbidden because by then people would know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds something new: the same act can become forbidden once it has happened before. After the first time, the crowd can be expected to realize what is going on, so it counts as knowing. The rule depends on what the people know, not on the act itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Flasks or leather containers
Market or main street
His public lecture
Like the case where the people know

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא changed his mind about the law. The law stayed the same. What changed is that the second time, people would know they were being used as a wall.

phrases.english: There were these flasks that were lying
in the market of Mechoza.
When Rava was coming back from his lecture,
phrases.notes: A big crowd walked with him. They became a wall of people without realizing it.

phrases.english: they brought the flasks in for him.
On another Shabbat they wanted to bring them in,
but he forbade them,
because it is now like the case where the people know
and so it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ זִיקֵי דַּהֲוָה שַׁדְיָין בְּרִיסְתְּקָא דְמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the same rule. It adds that doing it once can make people aware, which turns the next time into a case of knowing.
steps.raayaObject: A wall of people works only while they do not know. Once they can be expected to know, it is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling: he allowed it the first time and forbade it the following שבת.

steps.title: Sages who had things brought to them through walls of people
steps.stepSummary: לוי had straw brought to him, זעירי had fodder, and רב שימי בר חייא had water, all through walls of people who did not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: For לוי they brought in straw. For זעירי they brought in animal fodder. For רב שימי בר חייא they brought in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three more cases where great חכמים actually used a wall of people to bring things in. This shows that when the people do not know, it is allowed in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier stories showed when it is forbidden. These cases show the allowed side: important חכמים relied on walls of people who did not know. The list closes the discussion of walls made of people.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw
Animal fodder, a kind of grass for feeding animals
Water

steps.whatToRemember: A wall made of people works on שבת only if the people do not know they are being used as a wall. If they know, or can be expected to know because it happened before, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: For Levi, they brought in straw,
phrases.notes: In all three cases these things were brought in through a wall of people who did not know.

phrases.english: for Ze'eiri, fodder,
for Rav Shimi bar Chiya, water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two stories about when it is forbidden, this step gives cases where it was used and allowed, which closes the topic.
steps.raayaObject: A wall of people who do not know is allowed in practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of לוי, זעירי and רב שימי בר חייא.

steps.title: New משנה: someone who left with permission and is told it is no longer needed
steps.stepSummary: A person who left his תחום שבת with permission and was then told the matter was already taken care of gets 2,000 אמות in every direction from where he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone went out with permission. Then they told him, "The deed has already been done." He has 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. This person was allowed to go past his שבת limit, but on the way his trip stopped being needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person who goes past his תחום gets very little room to move. This משנה says that someone who left with permission is treated better: wherever he is when he hears the news, he gets a full 2,000 אמות in every direction.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (short for מתניתין)
Went out with permission, past his תחום
The deed has already been done, so his trip is no longer needed
2,000 אמות, the normal שבת walking limit
In every direction

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: how much room a person has once the reason for his permitted trip ends.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who went out with permission,
phrases.notes: He means someone allowed to go past his שבת limit for a good reason, for example to save a life.

phrases.english: and they told him: "The deed has already been done,"

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: he has two thousand cubits in every direction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic, not connected to the walls of people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who left his תחום with permission and is told the matter is already done has 2,000 אמות in every direction from where he is.

steps.title: If he is still within the limit, it is as if he never left
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if the person told to stop is still within the תחום, it is as if he never went out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was within the limit, it is as if he did not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds to the case from Step 10. If the man who was told 'it's already taken care of' is still within the תחום, we treat him as if he never went out at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 gave him 2,000 אמות from where he stands. This line adds a better result when he is still 'within the תחום': he is treated as if he never left. The משנה does not say which תחום it means, and the גמרא will soon ask about that.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת boundary: the 2,000 אמות a person may walk from his base
Inside the limit
As if he did not go out

phrases.english: If he was within the limit
it is as if he did not leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case of the man told his trip is no longer needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he is within the תחום, he is treated as if he never left.

steps.title: Everyone who goes out to rescue may return to his place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a general rule: people who leave their תחום to rescue others may go back home.
steps.simpleTranslation: All who go out to rescue return to their places.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a broad rule. Anyone who went beyond his limit on שבת to save people may come back to where he started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of step 10, a person who left with permission gets only 2,000 אמות from where he now stands. Rescuers get more: they may go all the way back to their original place.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go out
To rescue or save
They return to their places

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two rules: being 'within the תחום' counts as never having left, and rescuers may always return home.

phrases.english: All those who go out to rescue
return to their places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new general rule closing the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who leave their תחום to rescue may return to their original places.

steps.title: What does 'as if he never left' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'if he was within the limit, it is as if he did not leave.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'If he was within the limit, it is as if he did not leave'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the first line of the משנה from Step 11. It is setting up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the line seems to say nothing: if he is still inside his limit, of course he hasn't left it. So the גמרא wants to know what new point the משנה is making.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא; the discussion on the משנה starts here
What? What does it mean?
Left, went out

phrases.english: Gemara: What is meant by
'If he was within the limit,
it is as if he did not leave'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִם הָיָה בְּתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם כְּאִילּוּ לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the משנה line in Step 11 means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the line 'it is as if he did not leave' teaches, since read plainly it seems obvious

steps.title: רבה: It is as if he never left his house
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that a person still inside his own original תחום is treated as if he never left his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is what it means. If he was within his own limit, it is as if he never left his house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. 'The limit' means the person's own original limit, and 'as if he did not leave' means he is treated as if he never stepped out of his house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gets his full 2,000 אמות in every direction measured from his house, just like before he set out. He does not get just 2,000 from the spot where he heard the news.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (an explanation of the text)
His own original limit
His house
He is treated as, it is like

phrases.english: Rabba said: This is what it is saying:
If he was within his own limit,
it is as if he did not go out
from his house, that is how he is regarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If he is inside his original תחום, he is treated as if he never left his house and keeps his 2,000 אמות from home.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: of course someone still inside his limit keeps his home base.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה. If he never even got past his own limit, why would the משנה need to say he still counts as being at home?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says רבה's reading leaves the משנה teaching something too simple to need saying. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: Is it not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's explanation in Step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he never left his own limit, it is self-evident that he keeps his home base, so the משנה would have no reason to say it.

steps.title: We might have thought setting out cancelled his home base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we might have thought that once he set out to leave, he gave up his home base. The משנה teaches that he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he uprooted himself, he is uprooted. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה. It is not obvious, because someone might think that starting the trip cancelled his home as his שבת base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea is this: he left his house meaning to go far away, so he 'uprooted' his base. Then he would only get 2,000 אמות from where he heard the news. The משנה teaches that this is wrong: he still measures from his house.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first thought)
Since
He uprooted, gave up his base
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, setting out does not cancel a person's home base as long as he is still inside his original תחום.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since he uprooted himself, he is uprooted,
phrases.notes: He means that leaving home with the plan to go far away cancels his house as his שבת base.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הוֹאִיל וְעָקַר עָקַר קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a wrong idea was possible, so the משנה needed to teach this
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he set out to leave, he gave up his home base and would only get 2,000 אמות from where he stands.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not give up his base. He is treated as if he never left his house.

steps.title: רב שימי בר חייא: The new limit overlaps the old one
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא explains the משנה differently: the man is already outside his original limit, but his new 2,000 אמות reach back into it, so it is as if he never left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: This is what it means. If the limits that the חכמים gave him are swallowed up inside his original limit, it is as if he never left his limit.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives a different reading of the same משנה line. Here the person has gone past his original limit, but his new area overlaps his old one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give him 2,000 אמות from where he is now. If that new area reaches into his original תחום, he can walk back into the old area and is treated as if he never left it, so he may return home. רבה was talking about someone still inside his limit; רב שימי בר חייא is talking about someone already outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: The new limits the חכמים gave him: 2,000 אמות from where he now stands
Swallowed up inside, overlapping
From his original limit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. רבה: he never got outside his original תחום. רב שימי בר חייא: he did get outside, but his new 2,000 אמות reach back into the old area.
steps.whatToRemember: Two readings of 'as if he never left': רבה says he is still inside his own תחום, so he measures from his house. רב שימי בר חייא says his new limit overlaps his old one, so he may go back.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ תְּחוּמִין שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: If the limits that the Sages gave him
phrases.notes: This is the 2,000 אמות from where he is standing, the rule from Step 10.

phrases.english: are swallowed up within his own limit,
it is as if he did not leave his limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 13, different from רבה's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about someone outside his original תחום whose new 2,000 אמות overlap the original area. He is treated as if he never left and may return.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבה and רב שימי בר חייא disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies under the two explanations of the משנה from steps 14 and 17. This line sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read the משנה as a man still inside his old limit. רב שימי בר חייא read it as a man outside his old limit whose new area reaches back into it. The גמרא now wants the principle that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they arguing about? This asks for the principle behind a disagreement.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבה and רב שימי בר חייא, from steps 14 and 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the two readings of the משנה to look for the principle behind them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that separates רבה's reading from רב שימי בר חייא's reading.

steps.title: Do overlapping limits count?
steps.stepSummary: One holds that הבלעת תחומין counts. The other holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that overlapping limits count. The other Sage holds that they do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole argument is about הבלעת תחומין, a case where one שבת limit lies inside another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי בר חייא holds that if the old limit falls inside the new one, the man may pass from one into the other. That is why he can say it is as if he never left. רבה holds that overlap means nothing, so he had to read the משנה as a man who never left his old limit at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Overlap of שבת limits: one 2,000-אמה area sits inside or overlaps another.
It is something real. It counts and we may rely on it.
It is nothing. It does not count.

steps.whyThisMatters: הבלעת תחומין is the key idea for the rest of this sugya. Every challenge that follows tests whether overlap works and when.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר הַבְלָעַת תְּחוּמִין מִילְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: One Sage holds that the overlapping of limits is something significant,
phrases.notes: This Sage is רב שימי בר חייא, whose reading in step 17 depends on the overlap. The other Sage is רבה.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that it is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר הַבְלָעַת תְּחוּמִין מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether הבלעת תחומין counts. רב שימי בר חייא says yes, and רבה says no.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבה from a cave case
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that overlapping limits clearly work in the case of a man who set his שבת home base in a cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: Don't you agree that overlapping limits count? Think of a man who settled for שבת in a cave that is 4,000 אמות long inside, while its roof is less than 4,000 אמות long. Doesn't he get to walk the whole roof, plus 2,000 אמות outside the cave?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's view that overlap means nothing. He brings a case where everyone agrees overlapping limits work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole inside of the cave counts as the man's home, so he may walk 2,000 אמות out from each of its two openings. On the roof, which is shorter than 4,000 אמות, the area from one opening runs into the area from the other. He may walk the entire roof only because the two limits overlap. So overlap must count.

keyTerms.meaning: A cave. Here it has an opening at each end.
Its roof, meaning the ground on top of the cave.
4,000 אמות, which is two שבת limits back to back.

steps.confusionAlert: The man set his שבת base inside the cave, not on top of it. The roof matters only as the ground he walks on after leaving through either opening.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
And do you not hold
that the overlapping of limits is something significant?
Now what if he established residence in a cave,
phrases.notes: Here שָׁבַת means he set his שבת home base there. It does not mean he rested.

phrases.english: which inside is four thousand cubits long,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל גַּגָּהּ פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים אַמָּה —
phrases.english: and on its roof is less than four thousand cubits —
doesn't it turn out that he may walk all of it,
phrases.notes: "All of it" means the whole roof.

phrases.english: and two thousand cubits outside it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרָא דְּהַבְלָעַת תְּחוּמִין מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's side of the argument defined in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that הבלעת תחומין is nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the cave case, the man may walk the whole roof only because the limits from the two openings overlap. So overlap must count.

steps.title: The cave is different: he settled inside partitions before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that overlap works only when the man settled inside partitions before שבת began.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה answered: Don't you see a difference between a man who settled inside partitions while it was still day before שבת, and a man who did not settle inside partitions while it was still day?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself by drawing a line between the cave case and the case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cave, the walls made the whole cave his home before שבת, so both limits were set at the same time. In the משנה, the old limit was set before שבת and the new one was set on שבת. רבה says overlap cannot join limits made at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: The space enclosed by partitions or walls.
While it was still day, meaning before שבת began.
It is different. Used to draw a distinction between two cases.

phrases.english: He said to him: Don't you distinguish

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הֵיכָא דְּשָׁבַת בָּאֲוִיר מְחִיצּוֹת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.english: between where he established residence within partitions while it was still day,

phrases.aramaic: לְהֵיכָא דְּלֹא שָׁבַת בַּאֲוִיר מְחִיצּוֹת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם?
phrases.english: and where he did not establish residence within partitions while it was still day?
phrases.notes: This is the case of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא שָׁנֵי לָךְ בֵּין הֵיכָא דְּשָׁבַת בָּאֲוִיר מְחִיצּוֹת מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cave case shows that overlap always counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Overlap counts only when the man settled inside partitions before שבת, so both limits were set at the same time.

steps.title: Does overlap never work without partitions?
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: is רבה really saying overlap never works when the man did not settle inside partitions?
steps.simpleTranslation: And where he did not settle inside partitions, does overlap not work?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רבה's distinction. This line sets up a new proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer means overlap would fail in every case without partitions set before שבת. אביי doubts that this is true and is about to bring a case to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: And where he did not establish residence there.

phrases.english: And where he did not establish residence, does it not apply?
phrases.notes: "It" means the overlap of limits. The speaker is still אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רבה gave in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that overlap works only when the man settled inside partitions before שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is doubtful that overlap fails in every case without partitions. The proof is about to come.
